arxiv-2110-08076.description: Abstract We present a model of a viscously evolving accretion disc around a magnetized neutron star. The model features the varying outer radius of the hot ionized part of the disc due to cooling and the varying inner radius of the disc due to interaction with the magnetosphere.

arxiv-2401-02204.title: The line bundles on the moduli stack of principal bundles on families of curves
arxiv-2401-02204.creator: Roberto Fringuelli, Filippo Viviani
arxiv-2401-02204.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Roberto Fringuelli, Filippo Viviani. Given a connected reductive algebraic group G G over an algebraically closed field, we investigate the Picard group of the moduli stack of principal G G -bundles over an arbitrary family of smooth curves.

arxiv-2502-10843.title: LEAPS: A discrete neural sampler via locally equivariant networks
arxiv-2502-10843.creator: Peter Holderrieth, Michael S. Albergo, Tommi Jaakkola
arxiv-2502-10843.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Peter Holderrieth, Michael S. Albergo, Tommi Jaakkola. We propose LEAPS , an algorithm to sample from discrete distributions known up to normalization by learning a rate matrix of a continuous-time Markov chain (CTMC). LEAPS can be seen as a continuous-time formulation of annealed importance sampling and sequential Monte Carlo methods, extended so that the variance of the importance weights is offset by the inclusion of the CTMC.

arxiv-2509-05608.title: Cross-Service Threat Intelligence in LLM Services using Privacy-Preserving Fingerprints
arxiv-2509-05608.creator: Waris Gill, Natalie Isak, Matthew Dressman
arxiv-2509-05608.description: Abstract The widespread deployment of LLMs across enterprise services has created a critical security blind spot. Organizations operate multiple LLM services handling billions of queries daily, yet regulatory compliance boundaries prevent these services from sharing threat intelligence about prompt injection attacks, the top security risk for LLMs.

pmc-11772189.title: The effects of growth hormone on the outcomes of in vitro fertilization and embryo transfer in age-grouped patients with decreased ovarian reserve: a prospective cohort study
pmc-11772189.creator: Jiexiu Chen, Xumei Kong, Zonghui Luan, Yu Qiu, Shiqi Chen, Jesse Li−Ling, Yan Gong
pmc-11772189.description: BackgroundGrowth hormone (GH) could improve the outcomes of in vitro fertilization and embryo transfer (IVF-ET) in patients with decreased ovarian reserve (DOR), but which age group will benefit the most has remained controversial. This study aims to explore the outcome of IVF-ET among differently aged patients with DOR treated with GH.

pmc-12423310.title: Integrated single-cell atlas of human atherosclerotic plaques
pmc-12423310.creator: Korbinian Traeuble, Matthias Munz, Jessica Pauli, Nadja Sachs, Eshan Vafadarnejad, Tania Carrillo-Roa, Lars Maegdefessel, Peter Kastner, Matthias Heinig
pmc-12423310.description: Atherosclerosis, a major cause of cardiovascular diseases, is characterized by the buildup of lipids and chronic inflammation in the arteries, leading to plaque formation and potential rupture. Despite recent advances in single-cell transcriptomics (scRNA-seq), the underlying immune mechanisms and transformations in structural cells driving plaque progression remain incompletely defined.

pmc-12424184.title: Cooperative Free Energy: Induced Protein–Protein Interactions and Cooperative Solvation in Ternary Complexes
pmc-12424184.creator: Shu-Yu Chen, Riccardo Solazzo, Marianne Fouché, Hans-Jörg Roth, Birger Dittrich, Sereina Riniker
pmc-12424184.description: Protein–protein interactions (PPIs) play an essential role in biological processes. Molecules that stabilize or induce PPIs in ternary complexes have received growing attention for their therapeutic potential in engaging “undruggable” targets and their high selectivity. Here, we investigate the thermodynamics of the cooperative phenomenon in ternary complexes.

pmc-12499467.title: One‐Pot Isothermal Nucleic Acid Amplification Assisted CRISPR/Cas Detection Technology: Challenges, Strategies, and Perspectives
pmc-12499467.creator: Hongyan Liu, Hui Yin, Leshan Xiu, Wenyu Wu, Qinqin Hu, Yingchen Xia, Brianna Garcia, Shamsuttiyeba Shifa, Hui Chen, Min Li, Kun Yin
pmc-12499467.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). The cutting‐edge CRISPR (Clustered Regularly Interspaced Short Palindromic Repeat)/Cas (CRISPR‐associated proteins) system, as an emerging molecular diagnostic technique, is driving revolutionary developments in the detection field due to its high specificity and efficiency. However, the CRISPR‐based assays typically require the combination with an additional pre‐amplification step based on isothermal nucleic acid amplification to meet the requirements of clinical diagnosis, which brings issues including complicated operation and the risk of aerosol contamination.

pmc-12631078.title: Development of a venous thromboembolism risk prediction model for patients with primary membranous nephropathy based on machine learning
pmc-12631078.creator: Lian Li, Liuyun Wu, Yin Wang, Hulin Wang, Xingyue Zheng, Lizhu Han, Qinan Yin, Xingwei Wu, Yuan Bian
pmc-12631078.description: ObjectiveThis study utilizes real-world data from primary membranous nephropathy (PMN) patients to preliminarily develop a venous thromboembolism (VTE) risk prediction model with machine learning. The aim is to improve the rational use of prophylactic anticoagulant therapy by predicting VTE risk in these patients.

pmc-13079473.title: Simon says “stay in touch”: Reachability moderates the effect of irrelevant spatial congruence
pmc-13079473.creator: Michael L. Paavola, J. Toby Mordkoff, Cathleen M. Moore
pmc-13079473.description: The Simon Effect refers to the finding that simple left-right manual responses tend to be faster and more accurate when the response and stimulus are on the same side (congruent) compared to when they are on opposite sides (incongruent) even though the response is determined by a non-spatial attribute (e.g., color).

pmc-13226440.title: Trauma patients ≥ 65 years old constitute 40% of severely injured adult trauma patients in Sweden – a 10-year analysis of geriatric trauma prevalence
pmc-13226440.creator: Sara Bredberg, Emelie Modalen, Charlie Jöneby, Denise Nilsson, Oscar Lapidus
pmc-13226440.description: BackgroundThe elderly population in Sweden is steadily increasing. Age is an independent predictor of mortality in trauma patients. There is growing evidence that geriatric patients constitute an increasing proportion of the Swedish trauma population. No studies have analyzed temporal trends in the proportion of geriatric trauma patients in the context of the national trauma population in Sweden.

pmc-13337841.title: A qualitative study exploring access to online hearing loss information and support for adults with hearing loss
pmc-13337841.creator: Alicia Zou, Tsz Yui Wong, Jessica Turner, Diana Tang, Duncan Meldrum, Elizabeth Davies, Kate Sheng, Simon O’Toole, Jane Lee, Liz Gill, Melanie Ferguson, Bamini Gopinath

pmc-13362933.title: Navigating Privacy in Facial Transplantation: Ethical Considerations and Institutional Strategies
pmc-13362933.creator: Hailey P. Wyatt, Alexis K. Gursky, Sachin R. Chinta, Alay R. Shah, Bruce E. Gelb, Eduardo D. Rodriguez, Laura L. Kimberly
pmc-13362933.description: Background:During the last 20 years, the novel and highly visible nature of facial transplantation (FT) has posed a dual and potentially conflicting obligation for FT programs: to disseminate findings for scientific advancement while respecting recipients’ preferences for privacy, given the significant public and media attention.

pmc-13385255.title: Cognitive function in patients undergoing robotic radical prostatectomy – 1 year follow up
pmc-13385255.creator: Alicja Popiołek, Bartosz Brzoszczyk, Jędrzej Borowczak, Joanna Bitner-Szulc, Joanna Popławska, Piotr Jarzemski, Alina Borkowska, Maciej Bieliński
pmc-13385255.description: Postoperative neurocognitive disorders are clinically relevant, yet longitudinal data in patients undergoing radical prostatectomy are limited. This study aimed to evaluate longitudinal changes in cognitive function and identify factors associated with cognitive trajectories in patients undergoing robotic radical prostatectomy for prostate cancer. The study included 66 patients undergoing robotic radical prostatectomy for prostate cancer.

pmc-13554866.title: Left Atrial Appendage Outpouching Mimicking Coronary Artery Aneurysm on Pediatric Echocardiography
pmc-13554866.creator: Michal Huml, Tereza Fremuthová, Jiří Ferda, Josef Sýkora, Jiří Fremuth
pmc-13554866.description: Image(s)Multimodality imaging of a tubular left atrial appendage outpouching mimicking coronary artery aneurysm on pediatric echocardiography.Case SummaryA 3-year-old child with a recent history of febrile illness of unclear etiology underwent transthoracic echocardiography during evaluation of a heart murmur. A tubular outpouching adjacent to the proximal left coronary artery raised concern for possible coronary artery involvement, including coronary artery aneurysm.

pmc-13612861.title: Circulating tumour cells for guiding antibody‒drug conjugate therapy: Role of artificial intelligence
pmc-13612861.creator: Vahid Yaghoubi Naei, Mehran Dabiri, Lihua Chen, Jiajia Li, I‐Han Wang, Gungun Lin, Majid Ebrahimi Warkiani
pmc-13612861.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Antibody‒drug conjugates (ADCs) represent a major advance in precision oncology, yet their effectiveness depends critically on adequate target antigen expression. Tumour heterogeneity and dynamic antigen expression during treatment pose major challenges for conventional tissue biopsies used in patient selection. Liquid biopsy components such as circulating tumour cells (CTCs) enable real‐time, minimally invasive monitoring of tumour burden, molecular characteristics and target antigen status.

pmc-13700353.title: Multi-omics analysis reveals MICB promotes cerebral atherosclerosis through FTMT suppression in NK and plasma cells
pmc-13700353.creator: Yonggang Dai, Ye Liu, Yunjun Yan, Haoran Ji, Hongya Wang, Xuewei Zhuang
pmc-13700353.description: BackgroundFerroptosis, an iron-dependent form of regulated cell death, is implicated in vascular injury, but how immune-related proteins modulate ferroptosis and cerebral atherosclerosis (CeA) remains unclear.MethodsWe performed multi-step Mendelian randomization (MR) integrating plasma proteomics, single-cell eQTL, and FinnGen CeA GWAS data. Mediation MR quantified the role of the ferroptosis regulator FTMT. Cell-type–specific MR was conducted across 14 immune subtypes.
